title: a guest with no session opens the link the newsletter carried and the withdrawal lands in the real backend

steps.name: the dispatched message names an origin that is not the API's
steps.detail: page https://localhost:3943, API https://127.0.0.1:5943, link on /preferences/unsubscribe with a 46-character fragment credential, from 2 dispatched messages

steps.name: the guest holds no session with the API
steps.detail: the browser holds nothing the API would receive

steps.name: open the link, exactly as the recipient would
steps.detail: the done card rendered on arrival, with no confirmation step

steps.name: the withdrawal crossed the origin boundary and was permitted there
the withdrawal opened no session, which is why it works at all
steps.detail: no cookie on https://127.0.0.1:5943 after the withdrawal completed; 3 analytics cookies on the web origin (finding)

steps.name: the credential is gone from the address bar
steps.detail: address bar reads /preferences/unsubscribe with no token

steps.name: the backend recorded the withdrawal, and the next campaign honours it
steps.detail: suppressions 1, next campaign — leaver Suppressed, control recipient ProviderAccepted

steps.name: a second click on the same link is still a done card
steps.detail: replayed through about:blank so the component genuinely remounted; still the done card

steps.name: arriving with no token at all is a stated state, not a blank page

findings.summary: the guest withdrawal page sets analytics cookies before any consent
findings.detail: The browser arrived at https://localhost:3943/preferences/unsubscribe holding nothing and left holding _ga, _gid, _gat on https://localhost:3943. That is the app-wide analytics plugin rather than anything Growth does, and it is out of this lane's boundary — but a consent withdrawal surface is the worst possible page for it to be true on.
